stories.title: Dozens die as dengue surges in Malaysia while vaccine uptake stalls
stories.summary: Dengue infections in Malaysia have surged 56.2 per cent this year, with 58,079 cases and 55 deaths recorded so far, even as take-up of the dengue vaccine remains low. Dr Shanmuganathan TV Ganeson, president of the Federation of Private Medical Practitioners’ Associations, Malaysia, said cost was one factor behind the low vaccine uptake. stories.title: New wave of youth protests hits India – this time schoolchildren are demanding better facilities
stories.summary: The day began like any other at the school. Obedient children trooped in on Aug 13 at the Government Higher Secondary School in Jodhavas in the north-western Indian state of Rajasthan. But on that day, they did not head for the classrooms. Instead, they plonked down on the school grounds, chanting “Fulfil our demands!” to protest over longstanding grievances, such as the lack of teachers, which had stunted their academic progress. Only six teachers had been recruited to handle academic requirements for around 180 children at the school; seven other sanctioned posts were vacant. Other complaints included inadequate classrooms and the lack of a dedicated playground for sports such as football. Government school students have similarly trooped out in many other parts of India demanding better educational resources and infrastructure. They have been encouraged by the infectious optimism that has rippled out from the recent successful protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in New Delhi, which ended in the resignation of India’s education minister. Among the protesting children at Jodhavas was Tannu Sharma, a 10th-grade student at the school, which enrols students in grades 1 to 12. “We have only three functional classrooms, and even they leak when it rains,” she told. The Straits Times on the phone. Teachers tried to pacify the children, many of whose parents stood outside the school in support, but they did not relent.

stories.title: Electrochemist Liu Jiawei moves from Singapore to Hong Kong to start her own lab
stories.summary: For materials scientist and chemist Liu Jiawei, moving to Hong Kong supported her pivot into launching her own research group. After a decade immersed in Singapore’s research ecosystem, Liu sought a transition that would keep her closer to family in mainland China while maintaining an international, high-standard research environment.
